newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-BOCA AND RIVER BEGIN WAR OF WORDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOCA AND RIVER BEGIN WAR OF WORDS.

text.p: Players from Argentina's most bitter rivals River Plate and Boca Juniors began their traditional war of words on Tuesday in the run-up to next Sunday's derby match.
"We can beat River with our shirts," said Boca's Argentine international defender Nestor Fabbri.
"No matter how well they (River) are playing, the thought of facing us is, in itself, a psychological blow."
Asked if he had recovered from an injury, Fabbri's team mate Julio Cesar Toresani replied: "I would play against River on crutches."
River Plate coach Ramon Diaz, who openly admits he hates everything there is to hate about Boca, aimed his verbal weaponry at rival coach Hector Veira, who has occupied the hot seat at both clubs.
"I don't understand Veira. You can't be coach of River and then of Boca," he said.
Enzo Francescoli, River's veteran Uruguayan midfielder, refused to accept that Boca's blue-and-gold shirts frightened him.
"I can't accept this story about one shirt prevailing over the other," he said. "It's not serious."
Otherwise, Francescoli poured cold water on the rantings of his colleagues, preferring the blander rhetoric usually favoured by footballers in the run-up to big games.
He admitted to the weekly magazine "El Grafico" that some comments were made just to increase the expectation.
Not even River's record of four wins and a draw in their five games could tempt him to join in.
"If we start believing in this story that we are invincible we will be halfway on the road to defeat," said the 35-year-old, who missed a penalty in Sunday's 1-1 draw with Deportivo Espanol.

Current form heavily favours River, who lead the Clausura championship -- the second of the two tournaments played in the Argentine season -- and had not dropped a point or conceded a goal until the weekend. They also have home advantage on Sunday.

Boca, who boast the country's biggest and most fervent support, have made a stuttering start to the tournament, once again frustrating fans who have recently become used to seeing them struggle in the middle of the table.
